speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are experiencing chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to help me identify the cause, how long have these symptoms been persisting?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Infectious Colitis (likely Campylobacter or Salmonella) secondary to recent camping exposure, with symptoms suggesting progression to Irritable Bowel Syndrome with Diarrhea (IBS-D) or Post-Infectious IBS. The key features are the relief of pain by defecation, urgency, mucus, and incomplete evacuation after a specific exposure event.

I have reached my diagnostic conclusion based on the history of exposure and classic symptom profile. No further questions or tests are required.
